Phase-in precedent: sector-by-sector timetables, collective agreements first, the public sector as model employer. Courts have upheld staged duties where the end point is clear.
state.quoted_reply:
Three points, phased. First, define the end point before you define the timetable — the 1931 precedent staged agriculture and shipping over ten years but fixed the terminus on day one [1]. A clear destination withstands review; a drifting one invites injunction.

Third, pilot the wards Amara flags, fund the handover month, then legislate the calendar. Sequence is the argument.
